question: Can NFRDI's NSAP Interactive Atlas supply reusable historical species evidence directly, and what official path does NFRDI describe for requesting nationwide multi-year NSAP data?

sources.title: NSAP Interactive Atlas launched
sources.additionalReference: NFRDI FY 2021 Annual Report, Capture Fisheries Research and Development section, printed p. 19
sources.finding: NFRDI describes the Atlas as a public information tool for monitored landed-catch data. The FY 2021 report describes region/species/year/month catch trends, reports, and a downloadable-report workflow requiring a free account and sign-in. These are descriptions published in 2021-2022 and do not verify the live app's current data date, current access rules, or current export terms.
sources.reuseStatus: No item-specific redistribution terms for catch records or exports were verified. Do not treat public dashboard access as permission to republish its underlying data.

sources.title: NSAP Dataset, eFOI request NFRDI-928916030137
locators: Public response timeline and NFRDI replies dated August 18, 2025 and November 4, 2025
sources.finding: A public eFOI case concerning a request for the latest five years of nationwide NSAP data directs users to the Interactive Atlas for maps, graphs, and dashboards. For the nationwide multi-year dataset itself, the visible NFRDI reply asks for a formal letter to the Institute and a specific use purpose. The portal marks the case successful, but the visible reply does not show that a raw or cleaned dataset was delivered; do not represent this as a data grant or API entitlement.
sources.reuseStatus: This is process guidance from a public NFRDI response to another requester, not a current approval for Bangwit. The 2025 office-holder/contact route may have changed and must be verified before sending a future request. No requester name or contact information was copied into project materials.

assessment.atlasRole: Potential discovery source for monitored landed catch and fisheries-management context; not a complete fish-biodiversity checklist and not a substitute for site-resolved ecological or occurrence records.
assessment.dataAccessPath: Use the public Atlas for whatever views and documented exports are openly available. For multi-year nationwide NSAP data, NFRDI's public 2025 reply described a formal written request stating the specific purpose. Ask for existing aggregate outputs, documentation, current access route, and explicit attribution/redistribution/public-display terms.
assessment.liveAccessCheck: The Atlas root https://nsap.nfrdi.da.gov.ph/ timed out through the page reader, a 25-second direct HTTP request, and a browser-navigation attempt on 2026-11-01. A timeout does not establish that the site is unavailable to an ordinary user. No sign-in, export, scrape, or dataset download was attempted.
assessment.dataInterpretationLimits: NSAP landed-catch data describe monitored fishery landings, not a complete natural distribution or capture coordinate for every fish. Keep landing location, fishing ground, capture origin, current presence, and biological/ecological evidence as separate fields. Do not use landed-catch summaries as natural-diet, bait, water-safety, or current legal-rule evidence.
assessment.requestDraft: national-nfrdi-nsap-dataset-request-draft-20261101.md; unsent; contains Joseph Lopez's project description and a placeholder for contact information, not an email address.

disposition.reason: Official sources provide a concrete discovery route and a documented written-request pathway, but the live Atlas could not be inspected and the raw national dataset was not granted or acquired. A transparent unsent draft is prepared so acquisition can continue without implying approval or reusing undocumented data.

nextAction: Joseph may review and send the unsent draft through a currently verified NFRDI channel. In parallel, continue region-by-region research using independently accessible sources; use Atlas outputs only after checking the current page, data period, site/gear definitions, and reuse terms.
